rule: -TU at the end of a word is the feminine nominal ending, so it can be taken off.
quote: TU AB69 B69 𐀶 /tu/ Feminine nominal ending
examples: JA-DI-KI-TU (p.6); A-RA-TU-ME "erṣetum, fem. + mimation" (p.37); KU-PA₃-NA-TU "+ -atu, feminine of KU-PA₃-NU" (p.38)

rule: -TA at the end of a word can write a feminine ending -at or -āt, so it can be taken off.
quote: I-NA-TA is certainly the Minoan doublet of Ugaritic Anat and Biblical Anath
examples: I-NA-TA read ʿInat (p.16); I-NA-JA-RE-TA read ʾinayirʾāta (p.38).  The paper states the same ending written -TE at A-TA-NA-TE (p.38, already R52) and -TU at KU-PA₃-NA-TU (p.38)

rule: RU can be taken out as the separate particle lū, "may, let". The paper describes it as inserted into the word.
quote: between U-NA and KA-NA-SI, yielding hunna lū kanasī
examples: U-NA-RU-KA-NA-SI (p.9); U-NA-RU-KA-NA-TI (p.40); U-NA-RU-KA-JA-SI (p.40).  R34 already gives RU the value lū; this makes it a piece that can be taken out.

rule: The middle consonant of a three-letter root can go unwritten when it is w.
allows: root C₂ = w may have no sign
examples: RU-MA-TA and RU-MA-TA-SE read rāmāh from √r-w-m (p.39); I-ZU-RI-NI-TA and ZU-RI-NI-MA from √ṯ-w-r (pp.38, 40).  The paper never states this; it is what its readings do.

rule: A root-initial n can go unwritten when it runs into the next consonant, which is then written as a doubled sign.
allows: root C₁ = n may have no sign when the next two signs are an identical pair
examples: TI-TI-KU read hittīkū (p.40); I-TI-TI-KU-NI (p.38).  The paper discusses the same assimilation in Hebrew at p.9 (*han-bayt > hab-bayt) and p.12.

rule: A U sign can write the root consonant w.
allows: U = w (as well as nothing, or a throat consonant)
quote: Cf. tG √n-w-y (3ms prefix ya-; same paradigm as A-TA-I-*301-WA-JA)
examples: JA-TA-I-*301-U-JA (p.39).  The paper says it is the same shape as A-TA-I-*301-WA-JA, where WA writes the w; here the U sits in that slot.  This is read off the paradigm, not stated sign by sign.

rule: A word can be a compound of two Semitic words, each with its own root. Both halves must spell a root.
allows: word = element₁ + element₂, each spelling a root
needed_for: JA-SA-SA-RA-MA-NA → √m-n-y; A-MI-DA-O, A-MI-DA-U → √ʿ-m-m and √y-d-ʿ; I-NA-JA-PA-QA → √p-q-ḥ (6 rows)
examples: JA-SA-SA-RA-MA-NA = yāšār + mānāh (p.38); A-MI-DA-O and A-MI-DA-U = √ʿ-m-m + √y-d-ʿ (p.37); I-NA-JA-PA-QA = √ʾ-n-n + √p-q-ḥ (p.38)
